statement: A margin sweep is a no-op for the depth-7 MTP arm, with one boundary exception. The margin-skip fast path is gated on `draft_n == 2` at ds4.c:66808, and `draft_n` is the number of MTP drafts generated per step, capped at `draft_cap = e->mtp_draft_tokens` (ds4.c:66722). Our depth-7 arm uses `--mtp-draft 7`, so `draft_cap = 7` and `draft_n` ends at 7; the margin-skip cannot fire, so the margin value never affects acceptance. The six reads of `mtp_margin_threshold` (66734 assignment, 66739 env override, 66745 need-logits, 66808 gate, 66814 comparison, 66843 timing print) split by the gate: 66814 and 66843 are inside the 66808 block, so outside that gate the only read is the `> 0.0f` test at 66745. That test is the boundary exception: at depth 7, margin 0 and margin > 0 are not equivalent -- a zero margin turns off logit computation during drafting, a nonzero one turns it on. Every nonzero value behaves identically; zero is a different arm. This is a throughput effect (work done), not an acceptance effect. A sweep of 0,1,2,3,5 on the depth-7 arm would produce a flat line with a single step at zero.

claims.statement: The margin-skip fast path is gated on `draft_n == 2` at ds4.c:66808: `if (!strict_mtp && draft_n == 2 && mtp_margin_threshold > 0.0f)`. `draft_n` is the number of MTP drafts generated per step, capped at `draft_cap = e->mtp_draft_tokens` (ds4.c:66722). Our depth-7 arm uses `--mtp-draft 7`, so `draft_cap = 7` and `draft_n` ends at 7. The margin-skip cannot fire at depth 7, so the margin value never affects acceptance.
claims.falsifier: If the margin-skip is not gated on `draft_n == 2` (or `draft_n` can equal 2 at depth 7), then the margin can affect acceptance at depth 7 and the 'no acceptance effect' claim collapses.

claims.statement: The six reads of `mtp_margin_threshold` are 66734 (assignment), 66739 (env override), 66745 (need-logits), 66808 (the `draft_n == 2` gate), 66814 (the comparison), 66843 (the timing print). 66814 and 66843 are inside the 66808 block, so outside that gate the only read is the `> 0.0f` test at 66745. At depth 7 the margin value is read only at 66745.
claims.falsifier: If there is a read of `mtp_margin_threshold` outside the 66808 gate other than the 66745 `> 0.0f` test, then the margin value affects behavior at depth 7 beyond the zero boundary and the 'only read is 66745' claim collapses.

claims.statement: At depth 7, margin 0 and margin > 0 are not equivalent. The `mtp_need_logits` test at ds4.c:66743-66745 is `mtp_conf_log || getenv("DS4_MTP_FULL_LOGITS") != NULL || (!strict_mtp && mtp_margin_threshold > 0.0f)`, so a zero margin turns off logit computation during drafting and a nonzero one turns it on. Every nonzero value behaves identically; zero is a different arm. This is a throughput effect (work done), not an acceptance effect.
claims.falsifier: If the `mtp_need_logits` test does not compare `mtp_margin_threshold > 0.0f` (e.g. it tests presence or a different threshold), then margin 0 and margin > 0 are equivalent at depth 7 and the zero-boundary claim collapses.
